correctness.rationale: For p>=2, any two positive projective nodes have potential max>=1/2 by evaluation at the heavier node and min<=2^(-p/2) by the midpoint of their longer projective-circle gap. The equal orthogonal rule has exact range [2^(-p/2),1/2] for all real p>=2 by convexity. Strict inequalities from nonorthogonality or unbalanced weights establish all equality cases, including p=2,4,6. The sign of 2c_p-1/2-2^(-p/2) follows from degree-three arcsine Lobatto exactness and cubic Hermite interpolation with sign of the fourth derivative; direct interval Rolle reasoning handles nonintegral powers at the endpoint. The norm identity is also reconstructed using thin rectangles. Reproduction checker verify.py executed and passed 7264 deterministic numerical comparisons. No computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Power-Cauchy brightness is a natural geometric observable of convex bodies, and a two-view rule is the minimal positive exact configuration at p=2. The complete continuous sharp superquadratic minimax classification fills the missing side of the already published subquadratic theory, not an arbitrary single exponent. The reentrant switch at p=4 and p=6 produces a structural, nonmonotone signed-error spectrum while retaining a globally rigid optimal node arrangement; both general minimax value and exact transitions are useful for design choice and comparison against projective and harmonic cubature.
